questions.q: What does a Discovery Schedule record actually control?
options: Nothing — Discovery runs continuously with no schedule at all
Which specific CMDB field each probe writes its result into
The exact CPU and memory specs of every server in advance
When Discovery runs and what IP range or network segment it scans
questions.explain: A Discovery Schedule defines the timing (e.g. nightly, weekly) and the scope (the IP range or network segment) of a scan.

questions.q: What is a probe, per this lesson?
options: A tool used only to detect whether an IP address is reachable at all
A record that defines which network segment to scan
A general term for any Discovery activity, with no specific meaning
A specific, targeted operation that collects one particular kind of information once a device is found, such as identifying the OS or inventorying software
questions.explain: Probes are narrow and specific — one probe gathers one kind of detail, like OS identification or software inventory.

questions.q: What is the real, phased order Discovery follows, per this lesson?
options: An initial scan finds what's listening, then Discovery classifies the device type, then it runs the probes appropriate to that type
Discovery runs probes first, then decides afterward whether a device exists
Discovery runs every possible probe against every IP address simultaneously with no classification step
Discovery classifies devices before scanning for anything at all
questions.explain: The phased process is scan (find what's listening), classify (what kind of device), then probe (gather type-specific details).

questions.q: Why does Discovery classify a device's type before running probes against it?
options: Because probes can only run before any classification occurs
Classification has no effect on which probes run
To make the scan slower and more thorough on purpose
So it only runs the probes relevant to that device type, instead of asking irrelevant questions like a switch's installed Windows software
questions.explain: Running every probe against every device would be wasteful and often meaningless; classifying first lets Discovery ask only relevant questions.

questions.q: Why might a single ServiceNow instance have multiple Discovery Schedule records?
options: Multiple schedules exist only to run the same scan twice for redundancy
Schedules are only needed for software inventory, never for OS identification
Each instance is limited to exactly one schedule, so this never happens
Different parts of a network may need different scan frequencies or different MID Servers to reach them
questions.explain: Different network segments or buildings often warrant their own schedule, especially when reached through different MID Servers.
